framework: China - Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content (Doc. No. Guoxinban Tongzi [2025] No. 2; in force 1 Sep 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: On user request, providers may supply generated content without explicit labels after the user agreement sets out the user's labelling obligations and responsibility for use, and must keep related logs, including recipient information, for at least six months.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Training, validation and testing data must be governed by documented practices including examination for biases and measures to detect and mitigate them; data sets must be relevant, sufficiently representative, as error-free and complete as possible, and reflect the geographic, contextual, behavioural or functional setting of intended use.
what_is_tested: Data quality, representativeness and bias of train/validation/test sets

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Real-world testing requires a testing plan submitted to the market surveillance authority and approved (tacitly after 30 days unless national law requires authorisation), registration with a unique EU identification number, and a duration of at most six months extendable by six more.
what_is_tested: Authorisation and registration of real-world tests

framework: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1755 (arrangements under Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 Arts 92(6), 101(6))
requirement_paraphrase: Independent experts evaluating GPAI models for the Commission must be independent of providers (shared ownership, governance, staff or resources and contracts with the provider over at least the prior 12 months are considered), declare interests, and keep confidentiality and information-security protocols; providers may submit reasoned observations on appointed experts; experts are selected by call for expressions of interest (standing list possible), directly from the scientific panel, or under the Financial Regulation.
what_is_tested: Independence and selection of external evaluators of GPAI models

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluations must be scientifically rigorous (internal validity, external validity, reproducibility) and use state-of-the-art elicitation that minimises under-elicitation and model deception (e.g. sandbagging), matching misuse actors' elicitation capability and expected deployment context.

The AI trustworthiness framework series is at mixed stages: Part 1 logging at stage 50, Part 3 human oversight at stage 40, Parts 2 (transparency), 4 (accuracy) and 5 (robustness) at stage 20; all flagged harmonised, none OJEU-referenced.
Recommends periodic testing of backup, recovery and rollback procedures for AI systems.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Set pass thresholds before testing (to avoid moving goalposts) and refine them after testing only on evidence; thresholds are specific to each app and organisation.
who_tests: Developer / deployer (each organisation sets its own threshold)

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, Consolidated Version No. 2, Regulation 10 (autonomous and semi-autonomous systems)
requirement_paraphrase: Deployer/Operator must provide on request evidence of algorithms that make the System seek human intervention where processing may have an unfair or discriminatory impact, together with a risk and impact assessment of unjust bias or High Risk Processing arising from the System's inputs.
what_is_tested: Bias/unfair-impact risk and impact assessment; human-intervention triggers
who_tests: Deployer/Operator (self-assessment, available to affected party on request)

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Toolkit (Digital Dubai consultation page)
requirement_paraphrase: Digital Dubai states the Executive Council advised that the toolkit is to be used by all public entities looking to implement AI systems.
what_is_tested: AI systems of public entities, via the self-assessment toolkit

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: Once released, keep ongoing performance monitoring with evidence that the system operates as expected; use managed release processes with the ability to withdraw and revert; monitor for model drift.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
clause_or_page: Appendix A.1.5 Structured Public Feedback, p.49-51
requirement_paraphrase: Describes participatory engagement, field testing and AI red-teaming as structured feedback methods; red-team quality depends on team expertise; diverse, interdisciplinary red teams with domain expertise are suggested; types are general public, expert, combination, and human/AI.
who_tests: Red teams (public, expert, mixed, or AI-assisted)
